/-!
# Erdős Problem 175

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/175](https://www.erdosproblems.com/175)
- [Sa85] A. Sárközy, *On divisors of binomial coefficients, I*, J. Number Theory 20
  (1985), 70–80.
- [GrRa96] A. Granville and O. Ramaré, *Explicit bounds on exponential sums and the scarcity
  of squarefree binomial coefficients*, Mathematika 43 (1996), 73–107.
- [Ve95] G. Velammal, *Is the binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$ square free?*,
  Hardy-Ramanujan Journal 18 (1995), 23–45.

Sárközy proved the assertion for all sufficiently large `n`; Granville--Ramaré and Velammal
independently proved the full range `n ≥ 5`.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos175

/--
Show that, for any $n\geq 5$, the binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$ is not squarefree.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos175.lean#L678"]
theorem erdos_175 (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) :
    ¬ Squarefree ((2 * n).choose n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos175

review.notes:
The file's sole declaration, Erdos175.erdos_175, faithfully states that every natural n ≥ 5 has a nonsquarefree central binomial coefficient. The source wording, both solution papers, and the research solved category agree. Mathlib's definitions have the intended meanings. Independent Lean checks proved positivity of the coefficient, the prime-square characterization of nonsquarefreeness, squarefreeness at n=4, and nonsquarefreeness at n=5; evaluation also checked n=0 through 20. The scratch file compiles successfully.

The exact linked external proof states the same unconditional theorem. Its source was inspected, but the external project and complete transitive axiom set were not rebuilt or certified. Live Erdős pages returned Cloudflare challenges, so the archived page was used alongside the primary solution papers. Sárközy's full text was inaccessible; the historical attribution is explicitly corroborated by both solution papers.

Detailed checks are in /workspace/review/audit.md and /workspace/review/scratch.lean. No review edits were made under the repository; the reviewed Lean file matches its committed blob.
